These latter compounds are all known to interact with High affinity cationic amino acid transporter 1, indicating a possible pathway through which 4-alpha-Methyl-5-alpha-cholest-7-en-3-beta-ol may influence the activity of this transporter. The consistent presence of this compound in the targeting network suggests a possible role in modulating the transporter's function, though the exact mechanism remains to be elucidated. The evidence is supported by multiple high-scoring pathways, indicating a robust association, but further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction.
